newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand halts second airport project.
newsitem.headline: Thailand halts second airport project.

text.p: Thailand's cabinet decided on Tuesday to halt an estimated 100 billion baht ($4 billion) second airport project and concentrate instead on expanding Bangkok's existing Don Muang airport.

Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh told reporters after a cabinet meeting that because the government had to exercise strict monetary discipline, the decision had been made to halt the second airport project.

In December, Italian-Thai Development Plc said it had signed a contract worth 11.65 billion baht ($466 million) to do earthworks for the the second airport project, which was to be built at Nong Ngu Hoa on 20,000 rai (3,241 hectres) of land on the eastern outskirts of Bangkok and completed by 2000.

"Due to finance problems, the government forsees that the Nong Ngu Hao project will not be completed on time. So in order to maintain country as a centre for the international air transport we had to seek the option to expand the current airport," Chavalit said.

The existing Don Muang airport sits on 800 rai (1,296 hectres) of land belonging to the Royal Thai Air force. The airport can handle a maximum of 31 million passengers and 600,000 tonnes of cargo per year.

The transport and communication ministry will set up a committee to study the plan to expand the existing airport. The cost and details of the expansion would be discussed later, Suvit Liptapallop, the transport minister said.
